payload.name: Count events with synonym and generic-object expansion
payload.description: Use when a question asks how many times a person experienced an event and exact-term searches may miss memories phrased with synonyms or generic objects.
content: When a question asks how many times a person experienced an event, after searching with the question wording, run at least one additional search using synonymous verbs/nouns (e.g., rejected, turned down, denied, setback; work, submission, project).
Do not require the exact object noun from the question; search with the subject plus the event synonym alone so memories using a broader object (e.g., 'creative work') can surface.

Before answering with a count, treat memories describing distinct occurrences separately when they mention 'another' occurrence, different dates, or different contexts, even if they do not repeat the same object noun.

solves: Counting repeated events can miss memories that use synonyms or a generic object noun instead of the question's exact wording. The diagnosed cause was retrieving only one of two rejection events because the second was phrased as 'another rejection ... creative work'. Applies to future count-of-occurrences questions where memories may paraphrase; not when only exact named instances count.
